summary: Swain County NC Forest Service tower on Frye Knob, built in the 1930s as a two-story house-style lookout; listed as a former site, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Built like a two-story house, with living quarters on the ground floor and the fire lookout on the second floor
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks the tower as removed without a date; the register describes the site as a former lookout

events.note: Register says 'Built in the 1930s'; only the decade is given, so 1930 stands for the decade

notes_for_editor: Fate and today are thin: Forest Lookouts marks the tower removed with no date, and the register's 2013 caption calls it a former site. No source describes what remains or whether the site is reachable, so no access level is recorded. Built year is decade only. Do not confuse with the Frye Mountain fire tower in Montville or Swan Island, Maine, which appeared in search results; it is a different tower. No photo was added.
